title: MMGraph-Agent: Agentic Multimodal RAG via Cache-Inspired Multimodal Knowledge HyperGraphs
claim: Existing pipelines suffer high construction cost, long-context overflow, and split offline/online training; our cache-based unified framework resolves each challenge.
layout: 2 columns by 3 rows, challenge left, solution right, dashed borders
description: The figure is split into a left column titled "Target Challenges" (grey tag) and a right column titled "MMGraph-Agent (Ours)" (pink tag). Both columns have three aligned rows, so each challenge faces its answer. Row (i): high cost of knowledge organization, shown as files turning into a knowledge graph with cost, time, workflow and labor icons. It faces zero-API, ultra-fast construction of a multimodal hypergraph drawn as a Venn diagram. Row (ii): long context in retrieval, shown as an agent running think/search steps with a limited context window. It faces cache-inspired reasoning with query, retrieval, summary and insert steps around a dynamic cache. Row (iii): unified training is hard, shown as separate offline-knowledge and web agents. It faces a single agent querying and inserting into both sources through a cache. Each row uses its own pastel header colour. Icons of robots, graphs and globes carry the story.
caption: Target challenges and MMGraph-Agent.
abstract: Driven by increasingly complex real-world applications, Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) has evolved from textual pipelines to multimodal settings, comprising two complementary dimensions: knowledge organization and retrieval enhancement. However, existing methods still face challenges of high construction cost, context window limitations, and the lack of unified training across offline and online knowledge sources. To address these challenges, we propose MMGraph-Agent, a unified multimodal RAG framework based on cache-inspired multimodal knowledge hypergraphs. MMGraph-Agent enables extremely lightweight hypergraph construction with zero API cost and dynamic memory-based retrieval that alleviates long-context issues. Experiments across offline, online, and joint retrieval settings demonstrate consistent improvements in performance, efficiency, and architectural unification. Our software and data are publicly available at https://github.com/LHRLAB/MMGraph-Agent.
